A fixed-depth causal softmax stack with Lipschitz blocks, layer norm \(\varepsilon>0\), bounded embeddings, and a uniform margin \(\gamma\) recognises only languages that are definite modulo length.

- **Flat scores** (NoPE, RoPE, floored QK-norm). For all large \(n\), membership depends only on \((n, w_n)\). One earlier token moves the depth-\(L\) state by at most \(C(1+\ln(n/p))^{L-1}D/n\). The Cesàro model matches this at \(\Theta((\ln n)^{L-1}/n)\).
- **ALiBi of slope \(m\).** Membership depends only on \((n,\) the last \(k\) symbols\()\), with \(k=O(\ln(C/\gamma)/m)\). One layer already forces the rate \(e^{-md}\).
- **Converse.** Every such language has margin \(1\) under a hard window. Periodic positions give the subclass \(n\bmod p\); an arbitrary bounded positional table gives arbitrary dependence on \(n\).
- **Decoder.** A full history cannot keep margin \(\gamma\) on a table that stays at the start of the context once the attended length passes \(n_0\). Emitted tokens rescue it only by carrying the needed row into the last token, or into the ALiBi window. A pin of length \(N\) escapes only for \(N<n_0\).

RoPE fits the flat bound because the rotation is orthogonal, so the logit ceiling and the Lipschitz constant do not depend on the lag. Bounded sinks do not escape. The bound stops if the logit range or the readout’s Lipschitz constant grows with \(n\), if layer-norm \(\varepsilon\) is \(0\), or if the margin holds only on a thin set of strings.
